extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors who typeset their own papers using TeX/Plain TeX
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for producing and laying out displayed mathematical formulas in TeX (one-line, multi-line, aligned, numbered, and very long displays), including spacing, alignment, equation-number placement, page-break control, and typographic best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-line display with $$
rubrics_metrics.description: If you type $$ (formula) $$, TeX displays the formula in display style, centering it on a line by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can display two short formulas at once by typing $$ (formula1) \qquad (formula2) $$. This produces two formulas separated by two quads of space and the whole centered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting ordinary text into displays
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to get text into a display is to put it into an \hbox; you can even have displayed text with no math at all by saying $$\hbox{Displayed Text}$$.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: $$X_n=X_k \qquad\hbox{if and only if}\qquad Y_n=Y_k\quad\hbox{and}\quad Z_n=Z_k.$$ or $$...\qquad\hbox{for all $n\ge0$.}$$ — using math inside the hbox is fine and mirrors the intended manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use spacing (\quad vs \qquad) to indicate relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \qquad vs a single \quad to show relative closeness of parts of a display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \qquad appears around 'if and only if' while a single \quad surrounds 'and' to indicate the X part is less closely related to the Y and Z parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation-number placement with \eqno and \leqno
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation numbers are given second and are placed at the right with \eqno or at the left with \leqno; numbers are math formulas typeset in text style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: $$(formula) \eqno(formula)$$ or $$(formula) \leqno(formula)$$. Everything from the \eqno/\leqno to the closing $$ is the equation number, so you are not allowed two equation numbers in the same display unless special techniques are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forcing equation number onto its own line
rubrics_metrics.description: You can force an equation number to appear on a line by itself by making its width zero (e=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: use \eqno\llap{$(formula)$} or \leqno\rlap{$(formula)$} which sets e=0 and triggers the special positioning rules where the number is appended as a separate hbox with an infinite penalty to prevent page breaks between it and the display.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX's display geometry parameters (\displaywidth, \displayindent, \predisplaysize)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a display begins TeX sets \displaywidth and \displayindent based on the current paragraph shape, and \predisplaysize to the effective width of the preceding line (or a sentinel if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values are used in TeX's centering/packaging logic; your macros can examine or change them to alter typesetting behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging and squeeze routine for wide displays
rubrics_metrics.description: If the natural width L'0 of the display plus the equation-number-related space q is <= Z (displaywidth), the formula is packaged in an hbox of natural width; otherwise TeX attempts to shrink the formula if shrinkability suffices, else e is set to zero and the formula is packaged possibly overfull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: e = width of equation number (if present), q = e plus one quad. This governs whether TeX will shrink glue in the formula or drop the equation number to treat it specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering rules relative to equation number
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX tries to center the display without regard to the equation number; but if centering would make the formula too close to the number (space < e), TeX centers in remaining space or places formula as far from the number as possible (the latter only if list h begins with glue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally d = (Z - L')/2; if e>0 and d < 2e, then d is reset to (Z - L' - e)/2 or to zero if list begins with glue. The computed d is used to shift the formula box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predisplay and postdisplay penalties and skips
rubrics_metrics.description: A penalty item of cost \predisplaypenalty is placed before the display, and glue specified by \abovedisplayskip/\abovedisplayshortskip and \belowdisplayskip/\belowdisplayshortskip is placed depending on \predisplaysize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX sets \predisplaypenalty=10000 to discourage displays at page top. You can change \predisplaypenalty/\postdisplaypenalty; e.g. $$\postdisplaypenalty=-10000$$ will force a page break (preferable to an immediate \eject which leaves unwanted glue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment displays (\halign) behave like vertical material
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment displays are processed as if the \halign had appeared in vertical mode; each row of the alignment is shifted right by \displayindent and the resulting vertical list v is wrapped with pred/post display glue and penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In alignment displays \displaywidth and \predisplaysize do not affect the result, though you can use those parameters inside the \halign. Alignment displays are treated as three lines for \prevgraf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \eqalign for multi-line aligned equations
rubrics_metrics.description: \eqalign constructs multiple equations aligned by markers & and ended with \cr. The result is typeset in display style and is a vertically centered box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General form: $$\eqalign{left1 & right1 \cr left2 & right2 \cr ...}$$. Use & to mark the alignment column (often the '=' sign). \eqalign can be used multiple times in one display (it is a vcenter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \eqalignno and \leqalignno for numbered multi-line displays
rubrics_metrics.description: \eqalignno works like \eqalign but lets you append equation numbers on lines by adding &{equation number} before \cr; \leqalignno places numbers at the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: $$\eqalignno{... &=(...) ;(4)\cr ... &=(...) ;(5)\cr}$$. Note: \eqalignno generates an alignment display 'to \displaywidth' (full width).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between \eqalign and \eqalignno (vcenter vs full width)
rubrics_metrics.description: \eqalign makes a single vertically centered box no wider than needed; \eqalignno generates lines that occupy the full display width (an 'alignment display').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: \eqalign cannot be broken across pages but \eqalignno can; \eqalignno can be used without numbers; beware that \eqalignno centers the set without regard to equation-number widths so overlaps can occur without error messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control page breaks in \eqalignno with penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: You can force a page break after a particular line in an \eqalignno by inserting \noalign{\break} after the \cr; you can prohibit all breaks by setting \interdisplaylinepenalty=10000 or enclosing in a \vbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \noalign{...} to insert glue or \break instructions between lines. Wrap in \vbox{\eqalignno{...}} to prevent breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \noalign{\vskip(...)} to adjust inter-line spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to move certain lines farther apart or closer together in alignment displays, type \noalign{\vskip(glue)} after the \cr for that line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \noalign{\vskip3pt} will put 3pt extra space between the lines. You can also change space before the first line in the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \displaylines for unaligned multi-line displays
rubrics_metrics.description: \displaylines lets you display any number of formulas without alignment; each formula is centered because \displaylines inserts \hfil left and right of each line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Override centering with \hfill to get flush-left or flush-right effects: $$\displaylines{...\cr ...\cr}$$.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic baseline opening (\openup \jot) for multiline displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiline display macros (\displaylines, \eqalignno, \leqalignno) begin with \openup\jot which increases \baselineskip so baselines inside displays are farther apart for readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't want opening, cancel it with $$\openup-1\jot\eqalignno{...}$$. \openup effects are local to the display group. \openup2\jot spreads lines by 2 extra units (plain TeX uses 3pt per jot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-formula breaking principle: break before binary operations in displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Although formulas within a paragraph always break after binary operations and relations, displayed formulas always break before binary operations and relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Break displayed formulas so that the second line begins with the binary operator (e.g. '+') rather than ending the previous line with it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation rule for lines broken before binary operations
rubrics_metrics.description: When an equation is broken before a binary operation, the second line should start at least two quads to the right of where the innermost subformula containing that binary operation begins on the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \qquad or \qquad plus alignment markers so the operator on the continuation line is visually set right of enclosing delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking formulas with delimiters: choose explicit delimiter sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Because \left and \right delimiters cannot be split across lines, choose delimiter size explicitly so matching delimiters across lines have the same size (e.g. \biggl ... \biggr).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example technique: use explicit \bigg/\Bigg/... variants on both lines and align with & markers to position the break.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-line form for very long formulas (almost flush left/right)
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-line form places the first part almost flush left and the second part almost flush right (one quad away). This is particularly recommended when the left-hand side is long (break usually comes before '=').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieve effect with \displaylines and \hfill: use \hfill and \hfill{} to place parts at left/right. Insert {} where needed so TeX treats operators as binary (e.g. put {} before a plus on continuation).

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX never auto-breaks displayed formulas — author should indicate breakpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX does not attempt to break long displayed formulas automatically because line-break positions depend on subtle factors of mathematical exposition; the author is generally the best judge of where to break.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule of thumb, break at the end of a natural 'phrase' (major bracket or structural boundary) to preserve intelligibility; indicate convenient points of fracture when writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic advice: prefer minimal notation and 'spoken' exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The best notation is no notation; avoid complex alphabets when possible. Adopt the attitude that written mathematical exposition should be like spoken explanation to a friend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fall back on symbolism only when necessary; adopt plain-language narration and avoid using beautifully formatted but confusing notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a personal notebook of solved typesetting recipes
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a personal notebook recording non-obvious formulas you have handled successfully, showing both final output and what you typed to get it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps you refer back to solutions for similar problems months later and avoids re-solving layout challenges repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \postdisplaypenalty and \predisplaypenalty to control encouraging/discouraging page breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Change \predisplaypenalty and \postdisplaypenalty to encourage or discourage page breaks just before or after a display; plain TeX defaults discourage top-of-page displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. setting \postdisplaypenalty to a large negative number will force a page break placing the formula at bottom; prefer adjusting penalties rather than inserting \eject which can leave unwanted glue.
